title: Union-Find (DSU)
tagline: Track connected components with near-constant union and find via path compression + union by rank.

intuition.analogy: Friend groups at a party: each group has a 'representative'. To check if two people are in the same group, you trace each up to their representative. To merge two groups, you point one representative at the other.
paragraphs: The Disjoint Set Union (DSU) data structure maintains a collection of disjoint sets and answers two questions blazingly fast: 'are these two elements in the same set?' (find) and 'merge these two sets' (union).
Each set is a tree where every node points to a parent, and the root is the set's representative. Find walks to the root; union links one root under another.

Two optimisations make it nearly O(1): path compression flattens trees during find (point nodes straight at the root), and union by rank/size always attaches the smaller tree under the larger. Together they give the inverse-Ackermann α(n) — effectively constant.
intuition.keyIdea: Represent sets as rooted trees; path compression + union by rank keep them flat for near-constant operations.

steps.title: Initialise
steps.detail: parent[i] = i for all elements (each its own set), rank/size = 0/1.

steps.title: Find with compression
steps.detail: Follow parents to the root, and re-point visited nodes directly at the root so future finds are instant.

steps.title: Union by rank
steps.detail: Find both roots; if different, attach the lower-rank tree under the higher; bump rank on a tie.

complexity.timeReason: Path compression + union by rank give the inverse-Ackermann bound, effectively constant.

pitfalls: Forgetting either optimisation degrades to O(n) per op on adversarial inputs.
Union without find-ing roots first corrupts the structure.
DSU handles merging well but not splitting — it's a one-way data structure.

dryRun.clickMoment: union(1,3) doesn't touch 1 or 3 directly — it finds their roots (0 and 2) and links them. All four elements become one component through a single root link.
